Today, Amazon-owned Ring announced its first-ever smart lock. It tackles a big issue that has plagued many smart lock owners: dead batteries. Ring has come up with a clever solution to the problem, and the new product will launch in the first quarter of 2027. Additionally, the company also unveiled several new security cameras with improved low-light performance.

Ring Smart Lock

The concept of a smart lock isn't new in itself, but what Ring wants to solve is the problem of smart locks running out of power. To keep you from getting locked out at an inconvenient time, the Ring Smart Lock lets you hand-turn a knob on the back of the lock several times to generate enough power to run the lock for a while, so you can open the door and get back inside.

The Ring Smart Lock comes with all the features you'd expect from a smart lock. You can unlock it with a fingerprint, a tap-to-use numeric keypad, or via the Ring mobile app on your phone.

The Ring app also supports several handy features, including remote viewing and locking, or setting up scheduled or time-limited unlocks for family members or other visitors. You can also connect it with Amazon Echo and other Ring doorbells and cameras you may already have at home.

The lock comes in three colors—black, silver, and brass—and requires no extra wiring. It will go on sale early next year for $249. You can learn more here.

New 4K Cameras

In addition to its first smart lock, Ring also launched several new 4K cameras supporting the new Retinal Vision 4K standard, meaning you can get clear, color-accurate footage even in low-light environments. All of the following products are available for pre-order or on sale starting today:

  • Outdoor Cam 4K Plus: 140-degree wide-angle lens, with multiple power options including battery, plug-in, direct wired, and Power over Ethernet—$149.99 on Amazon, learn more here.
  • Floodlight Cam 4K Plus: Powerful floodlights, supports 24/7 continuous recording and smart detection, requires direct wired power—$219.99 on Amazon, learn more here.
  • Spotlight Cam 4K Plus: 550-lumen spotlight, 140-degree wide-angle lens, available in battery, plug-in, and solar configurations—$199.99 on Amazon, learn more here.
  • Indoor Cam 4K: Ring's first 4K indoor camera, supports dual-band Wi-Fi 6, with a 115-degree field of view—$99.99 on Amazon, learn more here.

Ring also launched the new Pan-Tilt Indoor Cam 2K for $69.99, bringing 360-degree panning camera capabilities to a more affordable price point. It can track motion and includes a privacy cover. You can learn more here.
